claims.statement: services/mcp-gateway is a Go sidecar that exposes the backend's provider-agnostic market data as an MCP server over the streamable HTTP transport at /mcp; it is a thin transport and client layer that holds no provider credentials, calls no provider directly, and reaches the backend only through the service-token data plane.
The MCP server identity reported at initialize is market-data-gateway version 0.0.1, and server.New registers every market-data tool by calling tools.Register with the MarketClient it closes over.
The /mcp listener is deliberately unauthenticated: the shared-secret trust boundary is the backend data plane, not the MCP transport, so the endpoint must stay on the internal network.

Browser cross-origin requests to /mcp are rejected with 403 Forbidden by wrapping the streamable handler in http.NewCrossOriginProtection, while non-browser MCP agents that send neither Sec-Fetch-Site nor a mismatched Origin connect normally.
Idle MCP sessions are closed after SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT because the streamable HTTP handler is built with mcp.StreamableHTTPOptions{SessionTimeout: cfg.SessionIdleTimeout}.
GET /health is the only other endpoint: it returns a fixed 200 {"status":"ok"} that does not depend on backend reachability, and any other method returns 405 with Allow: GET.

The HTTP server sets ReadTimeout 15s and IdleTimeout 60s but WriteTimeout 0, because the MCP streamable transport keeps SSE responses open for the session lifetime and any finite write deadline would truncate them; shutdown is signal-driven with a 10-second grace period.

All outbound backend communication flows through one Transport that owns a single http.Client with a 15s default timeout, a semaphore channel sized by MAX_CONCURRENCY bounding concurrency across all route groups, an 8 MiB response-body cap, 512-character detail truncation, and ValidateBaseURL startup validation of the backend origin.

RouteGroup isolates a data domain's path prefix and service token on top of the shared Transport; Do composes baseURL + prefix + path, URL-encodes the query, serializes a non-nil body as JSON with Content-Type application/json, always sets Accept: application/json, sets X-Service-Token when the group token is non-empty, and decodes a 2xx JSON body into out, while Get and Post are thin wrappers over Do.

Concurrency bounding is explicit: Do first attempts a non-blocking semaphore acquire, and on saturation emits a WARN record "backend concurrency limit reached, queuing call" before blocking on the acquire raced against ctx.Done(), so a queued call whose context expires returns ErrProvider with the context error as diagnostic detail instead of hanging.

The client normalizes every backend failure into four sentinel classes: classifyBackendError maps 404 to ErrNoData, 422 to ErrValidation (populating the parsed validation message), 401/403 to ErrConfiguration, and every other status including 5xx and unexpected 4xx to ErrProvider.

backend.Error keeps Error() generic by returning only the class text and excluding status and body detail; Status() and Detail() exist for Go-side logging only, Unwrap() exposes the sentinel so errors.Is works, and ValidationMessage() is populated only for ErrValidation, so diagnostic detail never reaches an agent.

Validation messages are parsed from FastAPI 422 bodies whose detail is either a plain string or an array of {loc, msg} objects; leading request-location kinds (body, query, path, header, cookie) are dropped from each loc path, messages are joined with "; ", the result is truncated to 512 runes, and any unparsable shape falls back to the generic ErrValidation text.

The tool result contract is implemented once in runTool: ErrNoData becomes a successful CallToolResult whose text is "No market data is available for this request."; ErrValidation becomes result.SetError carrying the parsed agent-safe validation message; ErrConfiguration and ErrProvider become result.SetError with the generic sentinel text; and anything else becomes the generic "tool call failed" error.

A local input-validation failure in a tool's prepare method is reported through result.SetError with the locally synthesized message and logged at ERROR as ErrValidation with status 400, and the backend is never called.

Every tool is registered through addTool, which attaches ReadOnlyHint: true, IdempotentHint: true and Title annotations and lets the SDK infer the input schema from a typed input struct with jsonschema tags, so non-omitempty required fields (symbol, statement, expiry) are rejected by the SDK before the handler runs.

tools.Register fans out to four per-family registration functions — registerPriceTools, registerFundamentalsTools, registerOptionsTools and registerSymbolTools — each living in its own file under internal/tools, giving exactly eight registered tools: resolve_symbol, get_quote, get_price_history, get_fundamentals, get_financial_statements, get_option_expirations, get_options_chain and get_technical_indicator.

Each tool maps to one of the eight data-plane routes: resolve_symbol to GET /symbols/search?q=, get_quote to GET /quote/{symbol}?exchange=, get_price_history to GET /prices/{symbol}?from=&to=&interval=&exchange=, get_fundamentals to GET /fundamentals/{symbol}?exchange=, get_financial_statements to GET /fundamentals/{symbol}/statements?statement=&period=&limit=&exchange=, get_option_expirations to GET /options/{symbol}/expirations, get_options_chain to GET /options/{symbol}?expiry=&option_type=&strike_min=&strike_max=, and get_technical_indicator to GET /indicators/{symbol}?indicator=&period=&fast=&slow=&signal=&std_dev=&from=&to=&exchange=.

Input is validated or clamped in the handler before any backend call: symbols are required, at most 32 characters and must match ^\^?[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9.\-=]{0,30}$, the search query is trimmed to 1-100 characters, exchange must be one of NYSE, NASDAQ, NYSEARCA, AMEX, TSX or LSE, statement is income/balance/cashflow, period is annual (default) or quarter, limit is clamped to 1-20 with a default of 5, interval is day/week/month, expiry is a required YYYY-MM-DD date, option_type is call or put with strike_min <= strike_max, and the indicator enum plus period bounds (2-400), std_dev > 0 and from <= to are enforced.

Every client method normalizes the symbol to upper case, trims it and url.PathEscapes it before placing it in the URL path, and renders float filters without exponents or trailing zeros, so the symbol pattern's rejection of path separators and percent-encoded segments is reinforced on the wire.

Three tools reshape backend payloads instead of passing them through: resolve_symbol ranks candidates in four tiers and returns best_match plus at most 10 alternatives, synthesizing ErrNoData for an empty search result; get_fundamentals filters the aggregate to the requested sections verbatim and synthesizes ErrNoData when every requested section is null or absent; get_financial_statements validates each item's non-empty date and symbol headers, passes line items and unknown fields through untouched, and wraps them in an envelope echoing statement, symbol, period, limit, exchange and items.

A malformed-but-200 backend payload (for example a statement item missing its date or symbol header) is surfaced as the generic "tool call failed" result through the mapBackendError catch-all, never as a no-data success.

Provider-agnostic vocabulary is a hard constraint on the whole module: tool names, titles, descriptions, result strings, log lines, error strings and the README must never name an upstream provider data vendor, and the rule extends to the module's test files, which assemble the forbidden names from string fragments so the enforcement itself cannot leak.

Configuration is loaded with an injected getenv and fails fast: BACKEND_BASE_URL (validated as an absolute http/https origin with a host) and MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN are required, while PORT defaults to 8080, ENVIRONMENT to dev, MAX_CONCURRENCY to 10 (positive integer), SESSION_IDLE_TIMEOUT to 30m (positive duration), and DATA_PLANE_PATH to /api/v1/market/data with MARKET_DATA_PATH as an alias and DATA_PLANE_PATH taking precedence.

The service token value is never logged and never appears in an error message: config.Load returns errors that name the offending variable without echoing the token, the startup log record carries service, port, backend_url, data_plane_path, environment and max_concurrency but not the token or its variable name, and tests fail the build if either leaks.

Structured logging uses log/slog with a JSON handler at INFO under ENVIRONMENT=prod and a text handler at DEBUG otherwise, with LOG_LEVEL overriding the default; inbound middleware logs every request completion at INFO with method, path, remote_addr, status and duration, dumps method, path, headers, query and a 64 KB-bounded body at DEBUG in dev, and redacts Authorization, X-Service-Token, Cookie and Set-Cookie to "[REDACTED]".
The logging response writer implements http.Flusher by delegating to the underlying writer when supported, so MCP SSE responses are flushed immediately rather than buffered by the logging wrapper.

Tool and transport instrumentation is level-gated: tool invocations log tool and arguments at DEBUG, completions log tool, duration and the response payload at DEBUG, and failures log tool, arguments, error_class, status and diagnostic detail at ERROR, while outbound requests and responses log at DEBUG and non-2xx responses or transport errors log at ERROR with status, detail and url; ErrNoData is treated as a normal DEBUG completion rather than an error.

Dev Compose builds ./services/mcp-gateway, publishes it on 127.0.0.1:${MCP_GATEWAY_PORT:-8005} mapped to container port 8080, passes ENVIRONMENT, BACKEND_BASE_URL, MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN and DATA_PLANE_PATH, and waits for the backend healthcheck; prod Compose publishes no host port, names the container retail-portfolio-mcp-gateway, sets restart: always and asserts MARKET_DATA_SERVICE_TOKEN with a required-variable expression.

Both Compose files healthcheck the gateway with wget against http://localhost:8080/health every 30s with a 5s timeout, 3 retries and a 5s start period, and the image is a two-stage build from golang:1.27-alpine to alpine:3.21 that compiles a CGO-free static binary from ./cmd/mcp-gateway and runs it as the non-root appuser with EXPOSE 8080.

Adding a new tool domain is a three-step workflow that modifies no existing client method: add the domain token and prefix configuration in internal/config/config.go and create a RouteGroup from the shared Transport, add a domain client in internal/backend/<domain>.go wrapping that RouteGroup with typed Get/Post methods, then add internal/tools/<domain>.go with a register<Family>Tools function wired into tools.Register.

The routes and query-parameter names the client consumes are a frozen contract defined in src/market/data_router.py and published as the committed OpenAPI snapshot tests/market/contracts/data_plane_openapi.json, whose parity is verified from both sides by backend contract tests and by services/mcp-gateway/internal/backend/contract_test.go asserting full eight-route coverage, no undeclared or missing query parameters, negative drift rejection and matching exchange vocabulary.

The Go checks run on the host toolchain rather than the Docker test harness: just test-mcp-gateway runs go test ./... in services/mcp-gateway, just lint-go runs a gofmt -l check plus staticcheck v0.8.1 and govulncheck v1.8.0 over both Go modules, and the dedicated mcp-gateway CI job on Go 1.27.1 with a cache keyed on services/mcp-gateway/go.sum runs go mod download, go vet ./..., a gofmt check, staticcheck, govulncheck, go build ./... and go test ./..., independently of the backend and frontend jobs.

Go service conventions for the module come from services/README.md: an independent Go module with a cmd/<service> + internal/ layout, configuration via an injected Load(getenv) with fail-fast validation, slog-based logging, request-ID and graceful-shutdown conventions, and a multi-stage Dockerfile that builds ./cmd/<svc> for a minimal non-root runtime image.
